title: The fold — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
The fold — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the address. 11 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide); 1 rfl declaration(s) are listed and not sealed, by design. Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 7 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 111 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 11. Most binding: A (10), B (9), merkleFold (7), C (4), merge (2), perms (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: address.lean. Built on it: ledgerclaims.lean. Checking this cluster needs 3 file(s): src/proof/merkle.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to 05a04d64-88a2-82b9-8c59-f26c36cd4312. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (2, 0, 4, 5, 3, 0, 0). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: nim.lean (3 observed, 1.22 expected, lift 2.46), families.lean (12 observed, 5.13 expected, lift 2.34), address.lean (4 observed, 2.07 expected, lift 1.93). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.16; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.57. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 84.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the hash tree — Ralph Merkle, 1979 (thesis); CRYPTO 1987 Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. merge_agrees — merge A B = [181, 59, 237, 190, 211, 88, 129, 103, 143, 231, 158, 123, 139, 178, 38, 2] record
  2. empty_fold_agrees — merkleFold [] = [147, 146, 154, 45, 72, 16, 138, 198, 159, 50, 78, 208, 125, 158, 1, 108] record
  3. singleton_fold_is_the_leaf — merkleFold [A] = A record
  4. the_fold_of_any_single_leaf_is_that_leaf — [A, B, C].all (fun x => merkleFold [x] == x) record
  5. pair_fold_agrees — merkleFold [A, B] = [181, 59, 237, 190, 211, 88, 129, 103, 143, 231, 158, 123, 139, 178, 38, 2] record
  6. fold_is_order_independent_on_two — merkleFold [A, B] = merkleFold [B, A] record
  7. merge_is_order_sensitive — merge A B ≠ merge B A record
  8. sorting_is_what_makes_the_fold_order_free — sortB [A, B] = sortB [B, A] ∧ [A, B] ≠ [B, A] record
  9. the_permutation_generator_is_complete — (perms [A, B, C, D]).length = 24 ∧ (perms [A, B, C]).length = 6 record
  10. fold_is_order_independent_on_four — (perms [A, B, C, D]).all (fun p => merkleFold p == merkleFold [A, B, C, D]) record
  11. fold_is_order_independent_on_three — merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [A, C, B] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [B, A, C] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [B, C, A] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [C, A, B] ∧ merkleFold [A, B, C] = merkleFold [C, B, A] record
